messages:
chris: seeing a weird one — some EU clients are getting the wildcard cert served even though the SNI matches a service-specific cert. started ~15:00 UTC, traffic spiked during a scale event. anyone else?
ana: yup I saw errors in the SRE dash, 502s and certificate warnings from curl tests. looks tied to ALB listener rules.
tess: can you paste a curl that repros? and which ALB?
chris: curl -vk https://model-service.eu.redwood.internal/ -H 'Host: model-service.eu.redwood.internal' --resolve 'model-service.eu.redwood.internal:443:34.198.23.1'
chris: output shows Subject: CN=*.redwood.internal (wildcard), expecting CN=model-service.eu.redwood.internal
ana: infra-bot flagged a recent cert rotation for the wildcard cert at 14:56 UTC, but the per-service cert rotated earlier and should be higher priority.
infra-bot: Deploy event: cert-rotation-wildcard completed (14:56 UTC). Target groups recomputed by ingress-controller v2.3.1.
chris: my suspicion: ALB listener has an overlapping SNI rule ordering problem — when rules were recomputed during the rotation + a target group churn, priorities swapped so the wildcard rule ended up with higher precedence. result: ALB matches wildcard before specific hostname.
tess: that matches an older race we saw — ingress controller can create both "host-based" and "sni" rules; depending on creation order AWS assigns numeric priority. If wildcard is created last it can get a lower-number priority and win.
nana: can we confirm rule priorities? run: `aws elbv2 describe-rules --listener-arn <listener-arn> --query 'Rules[*].[Priority,Conditions]'`
chris: ran it, snippet: 
```
["1", [{"Field":"host-header","Values":["*.redwood.internal"]}], ...]
["5", [{"Field":"host-header","Values":["model-service.eu.redwood.internal"]}], ...]
```
chris: wildcard has priority 1, service has 5. that's the bug.
tess: How did wildcard end up with 1? Should be the other way. Did the controller treat the wildcard rule as "default" and then re-create it?
nana: logs show ingress-controller created model-service rule, then wildcard rule was synced after cert rotation. AWS seems to give the next available lowest priority; controller uses generated priorities to avoid collisions but this sequence makes wildcard earlier.
nana: quick mitigation: swap priorities manually or add an explicit rule annotation to lock priority for model-service. we can also add exact-match SNI condition which wins over wildcard if supported.
chris: manual swap worked — I updated priorities to put model-service at 2 and wildcard at 10. 502s dropped and curl shows correct cert.
tess: longer-term fix: change ingress-controller to reserve a priority range for specific hostnames, or ensure cert-rotation creates wildcard without touching rule ordering. file a bug for controller v2.3.1.
chris: raised issue #INF-2489 with logs and playbook.
nana: another edge case: some clients send no SNI (old clients). ALB then serves default certificate; make sure default cert is a safe fallback (we should prefer a non-wildcard default for customer-facing hosts).
tess: agreed — action items: 1) make manual priority swap permanent via terraform change for the ALB listener, 2) patch ingress-controller to prefer exact hostnames or reserve ranges, 3) update runbook for cert rotations to check rule ordering.
chris: added a temporary CloudWatch alarm on rule mismatch counts. will watch through next rotation. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026 (tls-routing-wildcard-priority). automated snapshot of ALB rules attached.
nana: nice. if anyone sees more 502s drop me a ping, I'll roll back cert rotation if needed.
tess: thanks team. I'll add tests to the next release that simulate concurrent cert rotation + rule sync.
chris: thanks — closing this thread once we have the terraform change merged.
